clue.text: Legal officials leaving out first sign

parts.note: 'not' can mean excluding, as in 'everyone, not the cat'
Aries is the first sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: Some officials of the law depart without the first omen or signal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Legal officials' reads as the subject, and the rest as what they do; really the rest is two pieces read as phrases.
explanation.definitionFit: Notaries public are lawyers who witness and certify documents, so they are legal officials.

clue.text: Almost kiss sailor for heavenly drink

indicators.note: almost means not quite complete, so the last letter of the synonym is lost

parts.note: to neck is to kiss and cuddle
a tar is a sailor

explanation.surface: Nearly kissing a sailor for a divine drink.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth nectar was the drink of the gods, so it is heavenly drink.

clue.text: Character in posh hat's energetic song

indicators.note: in means the Greek character goes inside the hat

parts.note: a top hat or topper is a formal hat
eta is a character of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A figure in a smart hat bursts into a lively song.
explanation.definitionFit: A toe-tapper is a catchy tune with a rhythm that makes listeners tap their feet.

clue.text: Vast enterprise collapses without English salespeople

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the rearranged letters surround the extra letter
a collapsing enterprise falls apart, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A huge business falls apart, with no English sales staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like an instruction to drop E, but it means outside: the anagram of VAST ENTERPRISE goes around E.
explanation.definitionFit: Sales representatives travel to sell a company's goods, so they are its salespeople.

clue.text: Distinguished the last of the explosive books

indicators.note: the last of points to the final letter of the following word

parts.note: a mine is an explosive device
NT, the New Testament, is a set of books

explanation.surface: The final volumes of a dangerous, explosive series are notable.
explanation.definitionFit: Eminent means famous and respected in a field, so it is a synonym of distinguished.

clue.text: Decorative artwork to do with Biblical character

definitions.meaning: a picture made of small tiles or pieces of glass set in a surface
an adjective meaning relating to Moses, as in the law of Moses

explanation.surface: An ornamental piece of art about a figure from the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiled picture is one sense; the adjective formed from the name Moses is the other, so both lead to the same word.

clue.text: Workplace do for the Liberal Democrats?

definitions.text: Workplace do for the Liberal Democrats?

parts.words: Workplace do for the Liberal Democrats?
parts.note: split 'Workplace do' into work, place and do: OP (a work), POSITION (a place) and PARTY (a do), describing a party not in government

explanation.walkthrough: An office party is a workplace do; the Liberal Democrats are a British political party usually out of power.
explanation.definitionFit: A party not in government, opposing the ruling one, as the Liberal Democrats long were in Britain.

clue.text: Flexible monster with tail up run to earth

indicators.note: run to means extended as far as, so the next letter follows
in a down clue the final letter is lifted to the top of the word

parts.note: the Gila monster is a venomous lizard

explanation.surface: A supple beast, its tail raised, chased into its burrow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with tail up' moves the A of GILA to the front, giving AGIL.
explanation.definitionFit: Agile means nimble and able to move quickly and easily, so supple or flexible.

clue.text: Covers North American up, surrounded by imitations

indicators.note: surrounded by means held inside the following word

parts.note: copies are imitations

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the letters are read bottom to top

explanation.surface: Imitations encircle a North American who has got out of bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Covers' looks like a verb, but it is the plural noun: overhead coverings.
explanation.definitionFit: Canopies are overhead coverings, such as cloth over a bed or throne.

clue.text: Put an end to tax on children

indicators.note: in a down clue on means placed above the children

parts.note: scot is an old word for a tax, as in scot-free

explanation.surface: Abolish the tax on children.
explanation.definitionFit: To scotch a rumour or plan is to stamp it out decisively, i.e. finish it.

clue.text: Nasty person gets record on credit note

indicators.note: in an across clue 'on' means the record is placed after the credit and note

parts.note: CR is the standard abbreviation for credit in accounts
E is a musical note
EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: An unpleasant character gets a recording onto a credit note.
explanation.definitionFit: A creep is an unpleasant, obsequious or sinister individual, a slang term for someone disliked.

clue.text: Start amending topic 9

indicators.note: amending means changing, so the letters of these words are reworked into a new order

parts.note: the figure 9 is written out as the word nine

explanation.surface: Begin by revising the subject of clue number nine.
explanation.walkthrough: The '9' looks like a cross-reference to 9 Down, but it is simply the number spelt out as NINE, which joins TOPIC as the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: An inception is the beginning or founding of something, a formal synonym for a start.

clue.text: A space underground for humiliation

parts.note: a basement is a room or storey below ground level

explanation.surface: Being sent to live in a cellar room is degrading.
explanation.definitionFit: Abasement is the act of lowering oneself or another in dignity, which amounts to humiliation.

clue.text: Sometimes opted to return with female farm animal

parts.note: she is the female pronoun

indicators.note: returning means the chosen letters are read backwards
taking letters only some of the time means picking every other letter of the word opted

explanation.surface: Someone occasionally chose to go back with a female farm animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sometimes' picks the alternate letters P and E from 'opted'; 'to return' then reads them backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheep are woolly livestock kept on farms, so they are a classic example of a farm animal.

clue.text: Cheerful ape — but weird

indicators.note: weird means strange or distorted, so the letters of these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: An exclamation: a happy ape, though a strange one.
explanation.definitionFit: Upbeat means optimistic and positive in mood, a near synonym for cheerful.

clue.text: Book about fish keeps being a best-seller

indicators.note: keeps means holds inside, so the fish contains the other pieces

parts.note: the hake is a sea fish
OT, the Old Testament, is a book of the Bible
C is short for circa, meaning about

explanation.surface: A book about fish keeps on selling well.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a popular fishing book; the phrase 'selling like hot cakes' explains the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that sell like hot cakes are bought eagerly, so a hot cake is a runaway commercial success.

clue.text: French writer with extreme lese-majesté no longer in charge

parts.note: and means together with

indicators.note: no longer in means the letters are now absent from the word

parts.note: lese-majesté is an offence against a ruler, and its most extreme form is killing the monarch

explanation.surface: A French author with an extreme insult to the crown no longer runs things.
explanation.definitionFit: André Gide was a French novelist who won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1947.

clue.text: This Roman sticks around for tricks and artifices

indicators.note: around means the sticks enclose the Latin word

parts.note: canes are walking sticks
hic is Latin for this

explanation.surface: A Roman hangs about scheming.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicanes are pieces of trickery or chicanery, deceptions used to gain advantage.

clue.text: Dissident woman's name seen in the mirror

parts.note: her is the possessive for a woman

indicators.note: a mirror shows writing backwards, so the word cite is reversed

parts.note: to cite is to name or mention

explanation.surface: A rebellious woman's name appears in the looking-glass.
explanation.definitionFit: A heretic holds views at odds with established doctrine, so is a dissenter or dissident.

clue.text: Blue bed keeps little dog going round

indicators.note: keeps means holds inside, so the bed contains the other piece

parts.note: a cot is a small bed

indicators.note: going round means turning, so the dog's name is reversed

parts.note: lab is short for labrador

explanation.surface: A blue bed holds a small dog turning in circles.
explanation.definitionFit: Cobalt is a deep, vivid shade of blue named after the metal's pigment.

clue.text: Boast detective invades personal space

parts.note: to crow is to brag or boast
DS stands for Detective Sergeant

explanation.surface: A bragging police officer gets too close to people.
explanation.definitionFit: To crowd someone is to press too close to them, intruding on their personal space.

clue.text: Gap right in the middle of California causes complaint

indicators.note: in the middle of means put inside the abbreviation

parts.note: CA is the postal abbreviation for California
a hole is a gap

explanation.surface: A hole in the middle of California triggers a protest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complaint' here means an illness, not a grievance.
explanation.definitionFit: Complaint can mean a disease or ailment, and cholera is a serious intestinal infection.

clue.text: American horseman forever exposing bits

indicators.note: bits of the phrase are taken, so the answer lies within these words

explanation.surface: A US rider is forever showing off parts of himself.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul Revere made a famous midnight ride in 1775 to warn of British troops approaching.

clue.text: Strongly desire company doctor

parts.note: a vet is an animal doctor

explanation.surface: A firm badly wants its own doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: To covet is to yearn for, especially for something belonging to someone else.

clue.text: Face protection from half a dozen special soldiers

parts.note: six is VI in Roman numerals
OR stands for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: Masks for six members of a special forces unit.
explanation.definitionFit: A visor is a movable shield on a helmet that protects the face.

clue.text: There's life in this bishop (knocked out before)

indicators.note: knocked out of shape suggests the letters of bishop are rearranged

parts.note: ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: A churchman, earlier floored, still shows signs of being alive.
explanation.definitionFit: The biosphere is the layer of earth, sea and air in which living organisms exist.

clue.text: Architect gets very sick finishing the city

parts.note: John Nash designed Regency London, including Regent Street
ill means sick

indicators.note: finishing points to the final letter of the word the

explanation.surface: An architect falls badly ill completing a city project.
explanation.walkthrough: John Nash was the architect of Regency London, including Regent's Park terraces.
explanation.definitionFit: Nashville is the capital of Tennessee, a US city famous for country music.

clue.text: Put up beams in the auditorium

indicators.note: an auditorium is where an audience listens, so the word is as heard

parts.note: rays are beams of light

explanation.surface: Install lighting beams in a concert hall.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise something is to lift it or erect it, i.e. put it up.

clue.text: Extremely angry, then, the others

parts.note: so can mean therefore or then
the rest are the remaining others

explanation.surface: Very cross, then, are all the rest of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Sore means annoyed in informal use, and the superlative form expresses the extreme degree of being angry.

clue.text: Deny game is fixed by satellite

indicators.note: a fixed game is rigged, so the letters here are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone denies a match is rigged by a satellite.
explanation.definitionFit: Ganymede is the largest moon of Jupiter, and a moon is a natural satellite.
